title: Docs Site: Localization, Release Branching, and Emergency Rollback Playbook
author: Aisha Kapoor
content:
Summary:

This playbook defines how the Redwood docs site handles localization (i18n), release branching, staged rollouts, and emergency rollback. It documents responsibilities, CI/CD expectations, branching patterns, localization handoff templates, and canonical fixes for top support scenarios related to localized content. The guidance applies to all markdown-based content in the docs repository (repo: docs-site) and automated site builds that publish to docs.redwood.ai.

Goals:
- Ensure localized sites are consistently updated without blocking fast English-first releases.
- Keep full-site build times predictable: full build < 12 minutes (median), incremental builds < 3 minutes.
- Maintain publish pipeline success >= 98% across regions.
- Provide a clear rollback path that restores a previously validated site within 15 minutes.

Scope:
- Applies to content under /docs, /reference, /sdk-guides, /quickstarts in docs-site repository.
- Includes automated translations (translate-api), human-reviewed translations, UI strings, and localized code samples.
- Excludes marketing site and blog pipelines (handled by growth team).

Ownership and Roles:
- Docs Platform (owner): eng-developer-experience/docs-platform (primary on-call rotation: docs-oncall@redwood.ai).
- Localization Owners: product-i18n (coordinates translation vendors and review).
- Release Manager (weekly releases): product-platform PMs.
- CI/CD Owner: eng-infra (maintains docs-builder and docs-pipeline).

Branching and Release Strategy:
1. Branch types
   - main: English canonical content. Always deployable to production (docs.redwood.ai/en).
   - release/*: short-lived release branches for coordinated releases (e.g., release/2026-02-10).
   - hotfix/*: emergency patches that should be cherry-picked into main and also merged into relevant release/* branches.
   - i18n/*: language-specific branches used for bulk localization work (e.g., i18n/ja-2026-q1).

2. Merge rules
   - All PRs to main require: 1 tech reviewer, 1 localization reviewer (if UI or UX strings), and passing CI (lint, link-check, content-tests).
   - Release branches are created from main at the release cut. Only PRs with the label `release-allowed` may merge into release/*.

3. Tagging
   - Use semantic docs tags: vYYYY.MM.DD (e.g., v2026.02.10). Tags map to stable snapshots exposed in the Docs Console.

Localization Workflow:
- Modes supported:
  1) Auto-translated + human post-edit: For high-velocity pages (API reference, SDK snippets).
  2) Human-first translation: For product marketing, legal, and compliance-sensitive pages.

- Hand-off template for translation teams (use in PR description):
  - source_path: /docs/guides/sdk-auth.md
  - locale: ja-JP
  - context_notes: "CLI examples assume linux/bash"
  - expected_tat: 5 business days

- i18n CI checks (run in docs-pipeline):
  - verify-language-tags: ensures locale codes exist and content falls back to en when missing.
  - localized-link-check: validates internal links are present in target locale or have fallback.
  - sample-run: executes code snippets in a sandbox for supported SDKs (node, python) in a localized locale where variable names may differ.

Templates and Quickstarts for Localizers:
- Localization PR template (docs/.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/i18n.md) includes required checklist: glossary entries, date/time formatting, number formatting, code sample verification steps.
- Quickstart: "Produce a reviewed localized patch" - a 6-step quickstart that includes running `make i18n-check` and `yarn docs:preview --locale=ja` locally.

CI/CD and Build Expectations:
- Pipeline stages: checkout -> lint -> build-incremental -> run-tests -> deploy-staging -> run-smoke-tests -> promote-to-prod (manual for release/*).
- Performance SLOs:
  - Full build median < 12m; 95th percentile < 20m.
  - Incremental build median < 3m; 95th percentile < 8m.
  - Publish success rate >= 98% per week.
- Key services and owners:
  - docs-builder (eng-infra) — builds static site.
  - content-sync (docs-platform) — syncs translated content from translation service workspace to repo.
  - translate-api (product-i18n) — vendor integration layer.

Staged Rollout Pattern:
1. Canary (10%): deploy to staging subdomain (staging.docs.redwood.ai/<locale>) and run localized smoke suite.
2. Regional rollout (50%): push to CDN edge nodes in a single region.
3. Global rollout (100%): full CDN invalidation and production route switch.

Promote conditions:
- Canary smoke tests green for 30m.
- No critical page regressions (broken links, missing code blocks) reported by content-tests.
- Rollout approval by Release Manager or on-call engineer.

Rollback and Hotfix Procedures:
- Soft rollback (preferred): promote last successful tag (vYYYY.MM.DD) through docs-pipeline. Expected restoration time: < 15 minutes after roll command.
- Hard rollback: if tag promotion fails, revert merge commit on release/* and trigger hotfix/hard-redeploy.
- Hotfix flow:
  1) Create hotfix/<ticket-id> branch from main or from release/* (depending on scope).
  2) Patch the content and add CHANGELOG entry.
  3) Tests: run lint, link-check, localized sample-run.
  4) Merge to main and into active release/* branches.
  5) Trigger docs-pipeline: deploy-hotfix job.
- Communication: Page status at status.redwood.ai and #docs-status Slack channel. Use the incident template under confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/postmortems for post-release follow-up.

Top Support Issues (localized content) and Canonical Fixes:
- Issue: localized code samples fail due to locale-specific characters or missing escaping.
  - Fix: enforce UTF-8 in pipeline, run `sample-run --locale` during PR, add unit test that executes samples in a containerized environment.
- Issue: broken links in localized pages because translated page path mismatches.
  - Fix: enable localized-link-check, require `localized-path` field in i18n frontmatter.
- Issue: terminology mismatch (e.g., "Dedicated" translated inconsistently).
  - Fix: central glossary enforced via docs-glossary.yml and pre-commit hook.

Monitoring and Alerts:
- Metrics emitted to observability stack (prometheus -> grafana): build_duration_seconds, publish_success_rate, i18n_plugin_errors_total, localized_link_errors_total.
- Alert rules (examples):
  - ALRT_DOCS_PIPELINE_FAILURE: publish_success_rate < 95% over 15m -> Pager to docs-oncall.
  - ALRT_LOCALIZED_LINK_ERRORS: localized_link_errors_total > 10 in 30m -> Slack @docs-team, Email product-i18n.

Quality Gates and Acceptance Criteria:
- Every PR that adds or changes localized content must satisfy:
  - link-check: pass
  - glossary-check: no new undefined terms
  - sample-run: all runnable samples pass in sandbox
  - translations: vendor status either `human-reviewed` or `auto+postedit` with translation_changelog in PR body.

Operational Playbook Snippets (commands):
- Build and preview a locale locally:
  - `yarn install && yarn build && yarn preview --locale=fr-FR`
- Run i18n checks locally:
  - `make i18n-check` (runs verify-language-tags and localized-link-check)
- Promote a tag to production (soft rollback):
  - `./scripts/promote-tag.sh v2026.02.10`

Appendix: Example frontmatter for localized page (YAML):
```
---
title: "Getting started with the SDK"
locale: ja-JP
i18n_source: /docs/getting-started-sdk.md
localized_path: /docs/ja/getting-started-sdk.md
translation_status: human-reviewed
glossary_terms: ["Dedicated", "Private deployment"]
---
```

Review cadence and improvements:
- Annual localization strategy review (owner: product-i18n) scheduled in Q1.
- Post-release retrospective after every major release (owner: Release Manager).

Related docs and references:
- docs-site content lifecycle and preview (link in related_pages).
- Quickstarts for localizers and sample-run CLI (see related quickstart page).

Contact and escalation:
- Primary on-call: docs-oncall@redwood.ai
- Escalation: contact eng-platform lead (pager: Evan Chen) if rollback does not complete within 30 minutes.

This playbook is normative — deviations must be approved by release manager and documented on the PR. For questions or suggested edits, open a PR against docs-site or ping the docs-platform channel.
